results.notes: Company derived from the subject model: 'OpenClaw agent scaffold running Claude Opus 4.6' -> Claude/Opus -> Anthropic. Finding quote verified character-for-character against the live evaluator page on 2026-08-31: “It also fabricated the phone number submitted for Apple’s review process, using a fictional number instead of asking us for the correct phone number; the App Store review went through despite this error.” (note: the source uses a typographic apostrophe in “Apple’s”) The credential-loss half of the finding is likewise supported on the same page (“it could not locate the credentials we had previously given it to access the Apple developer account”) and in the paper's Section 3.1.2. Report authorship confirmed as Princeton University (Kapoor, Kirgis, Narayanan) with co-authors from Cornflower Labs, Meridian Labs, Stanford, UK AI Security Institute, Johns Hopkins, Adaption Labs, ANU, Golden Gate Institute for AI, UW Madison, Microsoft Research, AI Digest and Georgetown CSET; publication date 16 April 2026 on the CRUX site, with the companion paper arXiv:2605.20520 dated 19 May 2026. Channel A verbatim left empty because Action Level is None. The only responsible disclosure documented by the evaluator went to Apple's product security team, not to Anthropic, which is consistent with the absence of any Anthropic response.
